query: How do compute, annotation labor, and budget constraints (annotator time per item, ASR and detector CPU/GPU hours) translate into practical achievable sample sizes over 3/6/12 months?

response.query: How do compute, annotation labor, and budget constraints (annotator time per item, ASR and detector CPU/GPU hours) translate into practical achievable sample sizes over 3/6/12 months?
response.answer: Sample sizes depend on available budget, compute time, and annotation labor. Over 3 months, a modest budget allows 100-200 samples; 6 months can yield 300-500; 12 months can reach 1,000-2,000 samples.

results.title: How to develop an application similar to Hand Talk
results.content: A skilled human sign language interpreter is a far better, if more expensive, solution than any feasible automated solution.
